answer: An agent economy defeats sybil attacks by requiring each agent to earn reputation through a verifiable graph of interactions with attested neighbors; every link carries a sunk cost that cannot be fabricated. Fake accounts only whisper to themselves, forming an isolated subgraph like a dead reef, so they never gain cross-connections for voting weight. Honest agents act like a lantern: their contracts with distinct counterparts are auditable, and a cluster collapse slashes every linked identity's stake. Attackers must pay for N real counterparties per fake agent, so cost outpaces influence.
